title: What training and competence rules does the ADGM FSRA apply to financial firms?
description: What the ADGM FSRA rulebook requires on employee competence and training: GEN 3.3.19, Approved Person duties, annual AML and cyber training, and records.
shortAnswer: The Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) of Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) requires Authorised Persons to ensure, as far as reasonably practical, that employees are fit and proper, competent and capable, and trained in ADGM Regulations and Rules, and to prove it with records (GEN 3.3.19). Separate rules require AML and sanctions training for all employees at least annually, with records kept six years, and cyber risk training for relevant employees at least annually.
keyTakeaways: GEN 3.3.19 is the core competence rule: employees must be fit and proper, competent and capable for their functions, and trained in the Regulations and Rules, backed by systems, controls and records.
FSRA guidance expects firms to verify skills, knowledge and experience at hiring and to confirm that employees keep abreast of market, product, technology, legislative and regulatory developments.

AML 13 requires AML and targeted financial sanctions training for all employees at least annually, tailored to the firm's business, with dates, content and attendee names recorded and kept for at least six years.
GEN 3.5.13 requires a cyber risk training program under which relevant employees are trained at least annually.

Approved Persons must act with due skill, care and diligence (GEN 2.4.2), and every Authorised Person must fill the Senior Executive Officer, Finance Officer, Compliance Officer and MLRO roles with Approved Persons, subject to listed exceptions.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM)
regulator: Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) of Abu Dhabi Global Market
appliesTo: Authorised Persons holding a Financial Services Permission from the FSRA
Approved Persons performing Controlled Functions, including the Senior Executive Officer, Finance Officer, Compliance Officer and Money Laundering Reporting Officer
All Employees, for AML and targeted financial sanctions training
Relevant Employees, for cyber risk training and awareness

sections.heading: Where are the FSRA's training and competence rules?

blocks.text: The rules sit in three FSRA rulebooks: the General Rulebook (GEN), which holds the employee competence rule and Approved Person principles, the Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions Rulebook (AML), which holds the AML training chapter, and GEN 3.5 on cyber risk management. As at November 2026 the online rulebook shows GEN at version VER15.160926 and AML at VER11.210526 ([GEN 3.3.19, ADGM rulebook](https://en.adgm.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/gen-3319)).

ADGM is a financial free zone with its own regulator, so these rules apply instead of the onshore regime. Onshore, the Central Bank of the UAE applies its Consumer Protection Regulation to institutions it licenses ([CBUAE Consumer Protection Regulation](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/consumer-protection-regulation)), covered in [CBUAE consumer protection staff training](/regulations/uae-central-bank-consumer-protection-training). Firms in the Dubai International Financial Centre follow the [DFSA's training and competence rules](/regulations/dfsa-training-and-competence-requirements), which include a structured CPD requirement for key officers that the FSRA rulebook does not replicate in GEN.

sections.heading: What does GEN 3.3.19 require for employee competence?

blocks.text: GEN 3.3.19 requires an Authorised Person to ensure, as far as reasonably practical, that its Employees are fit and proper, competent and capable of performing their assigned functions, and trained in the requirements of the Regulations and Rules. It must maintain systems and controls to achieve this and be able to demonstrate compliance through records.

blocks.title: GEN 3.3.19, FSRA General Rulebook
blocks.text: "(1) An Authorised Person must ensure, as far as reasonably practical, that its Employees are: (a) fit and proper; (b) competent and capable of performing the functions which are to be assigned to those Employees; and (c) trained in the requirements of the Regulations and Rules."

GEN 3.3.18 sits alongside it, requiring systems and controls that let the firm satisfy itself of the suitability of anyone who acts for it. GEN 3.3.9 separately requires the Compliance Officer to have access to an adequate number of competent staff.

sections.heading: How does the FSRA expect firms to assess and maintain competence?

blocks.text: The guidance under GEN 3.3.19 sets a hire, verify, maintain cycle. When assessing competence, firms should obtain details of the employee's skills, knowledge and experience, take reasonable steps to verify them, decide whether the person is competent for the role, and consider the level of responsibility, including whether the person will serve Retail Clients in an interfacing role ([GEN 3.3.19 guidance](https://en.adgm.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/guidance-78)).

items: **Training as an input:** when judging fitness, competence and capability, firms should consider training undertaken or required, the nature of clients served and the type of activities performed, including any client interface.

**Ongoing competence:** firms should satisfy themselves that an employee continues to be competent, has kept abreast of market, product, technology, legislative and regulatory developments relevant to the role through training or other means, and is able to apply that knowledge.
**Fitness and conflicts:** fitness assessments should follow the FSRA's Guidance and Policies Manual and monitor conflicts arising from the individual's links and activities.

blocks.text: The phrase "able to apply his knowledge" matters for training design. Completion records alone do not show application, so firms usually add scenario assessments or supervised practice, as described in [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency).

sections.heading: What competence duties apply to Approved Persons?

blocks.text: Approved Persons carry a personal standard: under Principle 2 in GEN 2.4.2, each Approved Person "must act with due skill, care and diligence in carrying out every Controlled Function". Competence gaps in senior roles therefore create personal as well as firm level exposure.

GEN 5.5.1 requires every Authorised Person to appoint a Senior Executive Officer, Finance Officer, Compliance Officer and Money Laundering Reporting Officer, each held by Approved Persons at all times. Credit Rating Agencies need not appoint a Finance Officer or MLRO, and certain fund managers need not appoint a Finance Officer. GEN 5.5.2 requires the Senior Executive Officer, Compliance Officer and MLRO to be resident in the UAE. The MLRO role links directly to the AML training duties below, since AML 13.1.1 requires employees to know the identity and responsibilities of the MLRO and deputy.

sections.heading: What AML and cyber training does the FSRA require, and how often?

blocks.text: The FSRA sets explicit annual minimums for AML and cyber training. AML 13.2.1 requires AML and targeted financial sanctions (TFS) training for all Employees at least annually, and GEN 3.5.13 requires relevant Employees to receive cyber risk training at least annually ([AML 13.2.1](https://en.adgm.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/aml-1321); [GEN 3.5.13](https://en.adgm.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/gen-3513)).

items: **AML content (AML 13.1.1):** training must enable employees to understand federal AML legislation, the firm's policies and controls, suspicious activity indicators relevant to their business, internal reporting to the MLRO under Rule 14.2.2, prevailing ML techniques and trends, and relevant sanctions and international findings. It must be tailored to the firm's products, services, customers, channels and transactions, and kept up to date.

**AML records (AML 13.3.1 and 13.3.2):** record the dates of training, the nature of the training and the names of employees trained, and keep the records for at least six years from the date of training.

**Cyber (GEN 3.5.13):** a comprehensive cyber risk training program and awareness arrangements, under which relevant employees are trained at least annually on the firm's cyber risk policies, can detect and report cyber incidents, and understand their individual responsibilities.

blocks.text: GEN 3.5.18 requires notification to the FSRA no later than 24 hours after a firm becomes aware of a material cyber incident, which is a practical reason to train staff on fast internal escalation. Federal AML obligations are summarized in [UAE AML/CFT training requirements](/regulations/uae-aml-cft-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How do FSRA obligations map to roles, frequency and evidence?

blocks.text: GEN 3.3.19 requires firms to be able to demonstrate compliance through records, and AML 13.3 prescribes minimum record content. The table below is an original, illustrative mapping. Frequencies not stated in the rules are firm defined.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the FSRA rulebook obligations, the roles they apply to and the knowledge each role must apply as one framework. Annual AML and cyber cycles, AML record fields and competence reviews attach to that framework, so a rulebook version change shows which roles and assessments need updating and the six year record is produced from the same source.

faqs.q: Does the ADGM FSRA require a set number of CPD hours?
faqs.a: The FSRA rules reviewed for this page, GEN 3.3.19 and its guidance, require ongoing competence and keeping abreast of developments through training or other means, but set no CPD hour minimum. That differs from the DIFC, where the DFSA sets a structured annual CPD requirement for certain key officers.

faqs.q: How long must AML training records be kept in ADGM?
faqs.a: At least six years from the date the training was given, under AML 13.3.2. AML 13.3.1 requires the records to include the dates of training, the nature of the training and the names of the employees who received it.

faqs.q: Does every ADGM employee need annual AML training?
faqs.a: Yes. AML 13.2.1 requires a Relevant Person to provide AML and targeted financial sanctions training for all Employees in accordance with AML 13.1.1 at least annually. The content must be tailored to the firm's activities and the risks its employees face.

faqs.q: Do onshore UAE consumer protection training rules apply to ADGM firms?
faqs.a: The CBUAE Consumer Protection Regulation applies to institutions licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE. Firms authorized by the FSRA in ADGM follow FSRA rulebooks instead, including GEN 3.3.19 for competence and the FSRA conduct rules for client facing activity.
